desc:
Given a string digits of decimal digits, decide whether it can be cut into at least two consecutive non-empty pieces so that the numeric values of the pieces, read from left to right, go down by exactly one each time (for example values 5, 4, 3).

A piece may start with zeros: the piece 004 has value 4, and the piece 00 has value 0. The pieces must cover the whole string.

For example "050043" works as 05|004|3 (values 5, 4, 3), while "1234" does not.
constraints: digits consists only of the characters 0-9
Piece values can be as large as 10<sup>19</sup>; in languages with 64-bit integers treat them carefully (the first piece can be up to 19 digits)
hints: Once you know the first piece, every following piece is forced to have a known value. So what is the only real choice?
Try every length for the first piece (it cannot take the whole string). Then repeatedly look for a next piece whose value equals the previous value minus one.

When extending the next piece character by character, its value never decreases (appending a digit multiplies by 10 and adds). Stop as soon as the value exceeds prev - 1. Because of leading zeros, a short run of zeros can be followed by the same value, so keep scanning until it exceeds.
editorial: Backtrack over the first piece digits[:j] for j from 1 to n - 1. After that, the next piece must be a prefix of the remaining string with value exactly prev - 1. Scan prefixes of the remaining text; when a prefix has the wanted value, recurse on the rest with that value; stop scanning when the prefix value gets larger than the wanted value. Reaching the end of the string means success.

The search is tiny. Only the first piece is a free choice, and later pieces are almost forced (several candidates exist only when leading zeros are involved, for example 0, 00, 000 all have value 0). The depth is at most n, so the running time is polynomial in n.

Take care of two edge cases: the first piece may not use all the digits (at least two pieces are needed), and a previous value of 0 can never be followed by anything, because the next value would have to be -1.
